messages:
mira: Heads up — a customer in eu-west reported a big latency spike and a bunch of 403 auth failures this morning. They say requests are routing to us-hosted pools instead of their dedicated eu cluster.
alex: which customer? any request ids or example traces? we need a repro request to follow logs.
mira: tenant: acme-analytics. I grabbed a few request ids from their app logs: r-0a1b2c3d, r-0a1b2c3e. Trace shows route resolved to hosted-us-west-2 pool, latency ~1.2s.
opsbot: Incident created: INC-2026-8742 — "acme-analytics: cross-region routing to hosted causing auth/billing/latency". Pager notified to eng-runtime.
jordan: I see related telemetry — pin refresh failures for dedicated eu pools between 06:10-06:25 UTC. TTL renewals returned 504 from control-plane for a subset of pins, so fallback logic picked hosted variant.
leo: quick note: fallback should pick regional hosted first; picking us-west is bad. Might be a routing table lookup that falls back to first compatible pool rather than region-aware.
alex: mira, can you paste the raw error from the SDK? also any header they send for region affinity? sometimes customers set X-Region incorrectly.
mira: customer said they don't set X-Region; using default SDK. SDK logs show: "route_resolution: pinned_eu_pool not found -> falling back to hosted_pool (id: hp-32d)" then auth returned 403: "token-tenant-mismatch".
jordan: 403 likely from hosted token binding — hosted pool expects hosted-scoped key; if token exchange failed we should have used dedicated with a short-lived hosted fallback token, not direct. Looks like auth token path assumed hosted ownership.
leo: could be a recent change in fallback flow (PR #4523) where we removed a verification step. Rolling it back for a targeted hotfix might help.
alex: repro steps (run locally):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <tenant-key>" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Tenant: acme-analytics" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-lite","input":"hi"}'
```
If control plane pin refresh is forced to 504, request should route to hosted pool. You can simulate by blocking control-plane at /pins/refresh.
mira: adding observed billing effect: customer was billed under hosted LB metrics between 06:12-06:24 for ~35k tokens — unexpected.
opsbot: Billing alert triggered: BILL-ALERT-3321 for acme-analytics. Notified billing-ops.
jordan: quick trace snippet from runtime logs:
```
[06:13:02] route_resolver: pin_lookup(eu-1) -> timeout
[06:13:02] fallback_decision: candidate(hosted-us-west-2) selected
[06:13:02] auth: exchange_for_hosted_token -> returned 403 {"reason":"tenant-mismatch"}
```
leo: action plan proposal:
- rollback PR #4523 on routing fallback (jordan)
- add region-preference check to fallback selection (alex)
- patch auth-exchange to have clearer error and fallthrough to retry with dedicated credentials (mira)
- billing reconcile request for acme-analytics and credit pending (leo)
- add alert when pin refresh failure rate > 1% for a tenant (jordan)

alex: assigned. I'll open a hotfix branch and try rollback first. jira: RUNTIME-2102.
mira: I will gather SDK logs and forwarded customer traces; will open a support ticket linking INC-2026-8742.
leo: billing-ops, please prep credit estimate — contact acme when we have root cause.
jordan: temporary mitigation: increase pin cache TTL for dedicated pools to reduce reliance on immediate refreshes. I'll experiment with 30s->120s for eu tenants.
opsbot: Update: deploy pipeline queued for rollback PR #4523 -> deploy-preview passed.
alex: rolling out rollback to canary 06:55 UTC. monitoring for route consistency and auth 403s.
mira: customer confirmed seeing reduced latency on a quick test. will let them validate for 30m and report back.
leo: excellent. follow-up items: postmortem with timeline, root cause, and improved tests for fallback ordering.
alex: tagging owners: @jordan (routing), @mira (auth/support), @leo (billing), I'll own rollback.
mira: thanks everyone. I'll keep this thread updated with customer confirmation and billing notes. :thumbsup:
